I recently went through an Amazon interview round and had to send my availability three times because none of my slots worked; with a Calendly link I could just pick a slot and only that one gets blocked.
I have used Calendly at work for the last 3 years. It's a lifesaver for scheduling two or more people with moderately busy schedules.
The paid plan only lets you configure one meeting configuration, so if you want to use it for personal life too you basically have to pay for it.
This is precisely the problem with Calendly and why I'd never recommend it - sending your calendly link signals the requestor is more important than the time picker.
Calendly still has the killer feature of being able to check multiple calendars to find scheduling blocks.

We pay 16/20 USD (yearly/monthly) per user per month to Calendly, and the only reason we pay for their Teams plan is that 'Round Robin' events are only supported there. I have zero loyalty to Calendly because I feel they are too expensive and would switch in a heartbeat.
Calendly is $8/user/month for essentials tier and $12/month for professional tier.

x.ai used to have manual confirmation before shutting down. We tried to raise this with Calendly but they refused: their answer was that manual confirmation only increases steps and eliminates email ping pong, which totally misses the point that my calendar isn't always perfect and I want to confirm meetings.
Every time I try to use Calendly, it fails because I've disabled Google Calendar from my Google Account.
savvycal.com is way better than Calendly.

I hate Calendly. The UI is nice, being able to pick a date is cool, and automated calendar invite does work. There is just something that tickles in the wrong way... It feels like a technological solution to a human communication problem.

I used to work at Calendly. One of the most powerful features we built was the ability to show availability both ways, so if the person booking also has Calendly, they see times where both parties are available, reducing back-and-forth.

Am I the only person who hates receiving calend.ly links? I find it somehow rude when someone asks me to go hunting around in their calendar, even though it's more efficient than agreeing on meeting slots.
There's a long list of simple features that calend.ly users have been asking for a long time... Top of my list: limit the total number of hours that can be booked per day.
I have such a small but annoying pet peeve about Calendly: if I try to type 'cal' into my browser, my calendar app always comes up first before the Calendly link.
I was using the Calendly free tier, and when a feature I wanted was moved off the free tier, it took me all of 30 minutes to move to zcal.

zcal is missing the ability to create a meeting 'poll' with all team members including external people that automatically considers everyone's availability, which is why we stay on Calendly for that feature.
